title: Vitamins
objectives: Understand the classification of vitamins as water-soluble and fat-soluble
Describe the chemical structure and biological functions of each vitamin
Explain the metabolic roles and coenzyme forms of vitamins
Analyze deficiency disorders and toxicity symptoms associated with vitamins

overview.title: Vitamin Overview
overview.content:
Vitamins are organic micronutrients required in small quantities for essential metabolic reactions in the body. They must be obtained from the diet as most cannot be synthesized in sufficient amounts. Vitamins are classified as either water-soluble (B-complex and C) or fat-soluble (A, D, E, K), based on their solubility properties which determine their absorption, transport, storage, and excretion patterns.

Biological Significance

  • Coenzyme Functions: Many B vitamins serve as precursors for coenzymes in metabolic reactions.
  • Antioxidant Protection: Vitamins C and E protect against oxidative damage.
  • Vision: Vitamin A is essential for phototransduction.
  • Bone Health: Vitamin D regulates calcium absorption and bone metabolism.
  • Blood Clotting: Vitamin K is required for synthesis of clotting factors.

Vitamin Classification

Water-Soluble

  • B1 (Thiamine)
  • B2 (Riboflavin)
  • B3 (Niacin)
  • B5 (Pantothenic Acid)
  • B6 (Pyridoxine)
  • B7 (Biotin)
  • B9 (Folate)
  • B12 (Cobalamin)
  • C (Ascorbic Acid)

Fat-Soluble

  • A (Retinol)
  • D (Cholecalciferol)
  • E (Tocopherol)
  • K (Phylloquinone)

key_concepts.title: Key Concepts
key_concepts.content:
Coenzyme Forms

B1: Thiamine pyrophosphate (TPP) in decarboxylation reactions

B2: FAD and FMN in redox reactions

B3: NAD+ and NADP+ in electron transfer

B5: Coenzyme A in acyl group transfer

Absorption and Storage

Water-soluble: Absorbed directly into blood, not significantly stored

Fat-soluble: Require bile for absorption, stored in liver and adipose tissue

Antioxidant Vitamins

Vitamin E: Protects cell membranes from lipid peroxidation

Vitamin C: Scavenges free radicals in aqueous environments

metabolic_roles.title: Metabolic Roles
metabolic_roles.content:
Energy Metabolism

B Vitamins: Essential for carbohydrate, lipid, and protein metabolism

Examples: TPP in pyruvate dehydrogenase, FAD in β-oxidation, B12 in methylmalonyl-CoA mutase

One-Carbon Metabolism

Folate: Carries one-carbon units for nucleotide synthesis

B12: Required for methionine synthase and folate regeneration

Specialized Functions

Vitamin A: Vision (11-cis-retinal), gene regulation (retinoic acid)

Vitamin D: Calcium homeostasis, immune modulation

Vitamin K: γ-carboxylation of clotting factors

clinical_correlations.title: Clinical Correlations
clinical_correlations.content:
Deficiency Disorders

B1: Beriberi (wet/dry), Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome

B3: Pellagra (dermatitis, diarrhea, dementia)

C: Scurvy (impaired collagen synthesis)

D: Rickets (children), Osteomalacia (adults)

K: Bleeding disorders (newborn hemorrhagic disease)

Toxicity Syndromes

A: Hypervitaminosis A (hepatotoxicity, teratogenicity)

D: Hypercalcemia, renal calculi

B6: Peripheral neuropathy (high doses)

Special Populations

Pregnancy: Increased folate to prevent neural tube defects

Alcoholics: High risk for thiamine deficiency

Newborns: Vitamin K prophylaxis at birth

faqs.title: FAQs
faqs.content:
Why can fat-soluble vitamins reach toxic levels while water-soluble vitamins generally don't?+
Fat-soluble vitamins are stored in body fat and the liver, allowing accumulation, while water-soluble vitamins are excreted in urine when in excess.
What makes vitamin B12 absorption unique?+
B12 requires intrinsic factor from gastric parietal cells for absorption in the ileum, and deficiency can result from pernicious anemia.
Why is sunlight exposure important for vitamin D?+
UVB radiation converts 7-dehydrocholesterol in skin to previtamin D3, which is then transformed to active vitamin D.
How does vitamin C function as both an antioxidant and enzyme cofactor?+
As an antioxidant it scavenges free radicals; as a cofactor it maintains metal ions in reduced state for enzymes like prolyl hydroxylase.
